report.summary: Chunk defines constants, helper functions _strip_human, _digest, and digest_ok. Public symbol: digest_ok. Claims checked.
risks: _strip_human | medium | Removes human fields but uses undefined constants FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS, AREA_HUMAN_FIELDS, ENV_HUMAN_FIELDS. | Verify these constants are defined in the module or imported.

_digest | low | Uses json.dumps with separators to produce canonical JSON; may differ from sorted-key JSON produced by other tools. | Confirm that the canonical JSON format matches expected digest inputs.
digest_ok | low | Docstring claims it checks if digest covers derived fields, but only function signature shown; implementation not in chunk. | Check implementation in later chunk.

handoff.purpose: Define constants and helper functions for stripping human fields and computing document digest.

claims.text: The mechanical projection of a whole document. Everything a human is allowed to write is removed: the human top-level blocks, and the human FIELDS interleaved into the generated records. What is left is exactly what this module derives, which is exactly what a digest should be a function of.
claims.why: The function removes _HUMAN_TOP_KEYS, and for areas, env_vars, repo_state it strips human fields or retains only head. The code matches the claim.

claims.text: A hash over the derived half only. Canonical JSON, sorted keys, so the value is a function of the content and not of the writer's key order.
claims.why: Function calls _strip_human to get derived half, then json.dumps with sort_keys=True and fixed separators, then SHA-256. Claim matches code.

claims.why: Only the docstring excerpt is shown; the function body is not in this chunk. Cannot verify behavior.

claims.text: orphan folds into island: both mean 'no entry point reaches it', and the map's own gate already merges them (drift.ISLAND_CLASSES). test modules are not features and are dropped entirely.
claims.why: References drift.ISLAND_CLASSES and behavior about test modules not in this chunk.

claims.text: Where the mechanically-detected staleness is filed. A distinct area so a reader can tell 'the tree contradicts this repo's own metadata' from 'this module is unreachable', which want different verbs.
claims.why: METADATA_AREA is defined as a constant string; comment describes its purpose, no contradiction.

claims.text: Directories a stale sweep must NOT descend into. Deliberately NOT the same set as reach._IGNORE_DIRS: build and __pycache__ are excluded there precisely because they are not source, and they are exactly what this sweep is looking for.
claims.why: References reach._IGNORE_DIRS not present in this chunk.

claims.text: The HTTP method a route handler implies. web_api dispatches on the request method by putting it in the handler's name, so this is a reading of the evidence rather than a guess -- and a handler that does not follow the convention yields '' rather than a fabricated method.
claims.why: The tuple maps suffixes to methods; if no suffix matches, the code would return empty string (not shown but implied by use). No contradiction.

claims.text: Starts at a letter or underscore so '/api/x' and '.claude/y' do not produce a phantom leading-punctuation token.
claims.why: Regex pattern starts with [A-Za-z_], matching the claim.

claims.text: The revision, and only the revision. branch and dirty move without the architecture moving, and a gate that goes red because somebody has unsaved edits is a gate people switch off.
claims.why: Function retains only 'head' key from repo_state, discarding branch and dirty.
